subject: Pilot credits extension and burn-rate check
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18 14:05 PDT
Subject: Pilot credits extension and burn-rate check

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps so we're aligned:

Call recap:
- Current pilot scope: assistive summarization across support tickets for ~5 product teams.
- Observed average (last 7 days): ~2.8M tokens/week (~11.2M tokens/month).
- Peak day observed: ~4.2M tokens (spike from batch process).
- Primary ask: pilot credits extension so your team can continue testing the higher-throughput workflows.

Pricing/qualification notes we discussed:
- Target unit economics you mentioned: ~$1,000 per 1M tokens (target for volume pricing) — we used that to approximate budget needs.
- At 11.2M tokens/mo that equates to ~$11.2k/mo run-rate at that target.
- You said your internal budget target for production (post-pilot) is ~$12-15k/mo, and you want to confirm viability before committing to reserved capacity.

Proposal & next steps:
1) Can you confirm the 7-day and 30-day token totals (we discussed a CSV export) — if you can attach the pilot usage report that helps our pricing team finalize the credit amount.
2) I’ll request a one-time pilot credit extension from my manager for 30 days while we validate steady-state burn. If approved, we typically offer credits sized to cover 3-4 weeks of observed burn.
3) If burn stays within the budget range and you want to proceed, we’ll outline a path to Reserved/Dedicated capacity (discounts scale with committed tokens/month).

If you’re good with that, please reply with the 30-day total and I’ll kick off the approval. I’m cc’ing Laura (manager) and Marcus (CS) so they have visibility.

Attachments: none yet — feel free to send the usage CSV.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189
From: Sam Patel <sam@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Janelle Torres <janelle@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-19 09:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot credits extension and burn-rate check

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. Attaching the CSV export from our pilot dashboard (pilot-usage-report.csv). Quick notes from our side:
- 7-day total (7/11-7/17): 2.8M tokens
- 30-day total (6/18-7/17): 12.1M tokens
- Typical steady-state looks like 3-3.5M tokens/week once we stabilize the batch ingestion.
- Budget: we can stretch to $15k/mo during evaluation but prefer to keep closer to $12k/mo for a multi-month commitment.

Can you and your team confirm what level of credits you’d be comfortable extending? Also want to understand whether credits can be applied to both hosted and dedicated capacity or only hosted.

Janelle (cc) — looping you in so you can confirm your internal timing for the extended test.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Integrations
Acme Health
sam@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20 11:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot credits extension and burn-rate check

Sam —

Appreciate the export, that’s perfect. I talked with Laura and Marcus about the numbers and here’s what we can do:

Approved pilot credit extension (one-time):
- 3,000,000 tokens of free credits applied to your Hosted account, valid for 30 days from the activation date.
- Rationale: covers ~3-4 weeks of observed burn (based on your 12.1M/month figure we expect this will give you room to exercise peak workflows without interrupting evaluation).
- Conditions: credits apply only to hosted API usage (we can apply a separate pilot arrangement for Dedicated/Reserved; that’s a commercial conversation).

Follow-ups & next steps:
- I’ve uploaded the pilot extension confirmation to the deal record in HubSpot (link below) and attached a short pilot credits agreement for signature (redwood-pilot-credits-agreement.pdf).
- Please sign the agreement (DocuSign link) so we can provision credits the same day we receive signatures.
- Marcus will follow up with a technical checklist for reducing peak cost (batching, prefix cache) and setting alerts if you hit >80% of credits.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/54321/DEAL-2026-0343 | DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC-123

If that works, sign the attached and I’ll confirm provisioning & activation date.

Thanks — cc’ing Laura for approval visibility.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Sam Patel <sam@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Janelle Torres <janelle@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-22 10:15 PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot credits extension and burn-rate check

Marissa —

This is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. I reviewed the agreement and Janelle will sign today via DocuSign. Two quick operational questions before we sign:
1) How are overages handled once credits are consumed? (auto-bill at list rate, or do you block usage?)
2) If we convert to Reserved capacity inside 45 days, can these credits be applied to the committed spend or are they strictly a one-time hosted-credit?

If you can confirm those two points I’ll sign and we’ll kick off the extended run.

Thanks,
Sam
